clues: A standardized three-phase perioperative communication protocol
Includes pauses called Sign In, Time Out, and Sign Out
Designed to prevent wrong-site surgery, retained swabs, and anaesthesia errors
A laboratory coagulation assay evaluating the extrinsic clotting pathway
Prolongs early in obstructive jaundice due to vitamin K malabsorption
Standardized internationally as the INR
An abnormal radiological finding in a patient with an acute abdomen
Seen as a crescent of dark gas beneath the right hemidiaphragm on an erect chest X-ray
Indicates perforation of a hollow abdominal viscus such as a peptic ulcer
A six-grade preoperative physical status scoring system
Grade I denotes a healthy patient while Grade V denotes a moribund patient
Used by anaesthetists and surgeons to stratify perioperative morbidity risk
A preoperative blood bank request for operations with low expected bleeding
Determines ABO and Rhesus status and screens serum for atypical antibodies
Unlike a full cross-match, it does not physically reserve specific donor blood units
A rapid outpatient diagnostic sampling technique using a 21G to 25G needle
Examines individual aspirated cells from thyroid, breast, or lymph node lumps
Cannot assess tissue architecture to distinguish in situ from invasive cancer
A life-threatening endocrine emergency during or after surgery
Occurs in patients on chronic steroid therapy whose HPA axis is suppressed
Prevented by administering intravenous hydrocortisone cover at induction
Targeted perioperative antimicrobial administration before bacterial contamination
Given intravenously within 30 to 60 minutes prior to skin incision
Reduces surgical site infections in clean-contaminated and implant procedures
An inflatable cuff applied to the proximal upper or lower extremity
Used after limb exsanguination to create a bloodless operative field
Contraindicated in severe peripheral vascular disease and sickle cell crisis
